The color of the leaf in the reference image is also different (brownish-red) compared to the green leaf in the test image, though this could be due to the age of the leaf or severity of infection.

Next, I will view a reference image for Powdery_Mildew. Although there is no description, the visual might provide clues.

thought
The reference image for Powdery_Mildew shows a leaf covered in white, powdery fungal growth, which is very distinct from the dark spots seen in the test image. This rules out Powdery_Mildew.

Finally, I will view a reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
The reference image for Sooty_Mould shows a leaf covered in a dark, superficial, blackish fungal growth, consistent with the description "Dark sooty deposits on the upper surface of leaves and stems". While the test image also has dark spots, they appear to be necrotic (dead) tissue within the leaf, rather than a superficial growth on the surface. The spots in the test image are also more distinct and defined than the more widespread, less defined sooty mould.

Revisiting Anthracnose, the description "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out" aligns most closely with the test image, despite the first Anthracnose reference image showing more advanced damage. The spots in the test image are irregular and dark, suggesting necrotic tissue. I will re-examine another Anthracnose image to see if I can find a better match before making a final decision, given I have one reference image view remaining.

thought
This second Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`) shows irregular, dark brown to black spots on a green leaf, which is a much closer match to the test image. The spots are distinct, irregular, and appear to be dead tissue, consistent with the Anthracnose description.

Considering all the evidence, Anthracnose is the most fitting classification.
